summary: Introductory discovery for Elmcrest Aerospace evaluating Redwood private onramp. Main focus: how Redwood Private would integrate into Elmcrest VPCs (peering vs private endpoints), egress/static IP needs for regulatory partners, regional restrictions for EU customers, and security/compliance requirements. Agreed to pilot and network benching; Redwood to share diagrams, security docs, and a Terraform example. Next meeting: bench test scheduling and pilot kickoff.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-06-27 15:00 UTC | duration 47m | attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Liam (Elmcrest Head of Platform), Priya (Security), Daniel (Network), Nina (Procurement)

[00:00] Sofia Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. quick round of intros. I'm Sofia, AE at Redwood. Marco is our systems engineer.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: Hey, Liam here. we run Elmcrest's platform infra; trying to figure out how to safely route inference traffic into our systems.
[00:25] Priya Menon: Priya - security. main concerns: data residency, KMS integration, audit logs.
[00:30] Daniel Park: Daniel - networking, i'll own the firewall and routing bits.
[00:33] Nina Ruiz: Nina from procurement - just making sure contract/submission timelines.
[00:38] Marco Alvarez: Awesome. quick orientation: Redwood offers Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. today we'll focus on Private — private control plane + private data plane options (interface endpoints, VPC peering, transit gateway flows), and typical egress patterns.
[00:52] Liam: Right, our legal team requires that inference traffic for EU customers stays in eu-west-1 and we need static egress IPs for our downstream partners. can you do static IPs in Private?
[01:05] Marco: short answer: yes, usually via NAT gateway egress IPs or using our egress proxy in the customer's VPC. there are a couple patterns: 1) Private Endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) — you create interface endpoints in your VPC; traffic stays on the AWS network. 2) VPC peering — direct peering but you'll need route table changes and management overhead. 3) Transit Gateway — for multi-VPC architectures. each has tradeoffs.
[01:34] Priya: quick interruption — for KMS, we want BYOK with HSM-backed keys and audit logs pushed to our SIEM. does Redwood support CMKs in customer KMS?
[01:45] Sofia: yes, our Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS keys; we can integrate with AWS KMS and HSM providers. audit logs can be forwarded; we currently have integrations customers use to stream logs to S3 or to SIEM via our log-forwarder. we'll send the whitepaper.
[01:58] Daniel: how about IP ranges? we need predictable CIDRs for firewall policies. can you publish your ranges?
[02:06] Marco: in Private we normally don't need Redwood-owned public IPs inside your VPC because you create interface endpoints or peering; but for egress to third parties we can allocate static egress IPs in your account or via a managed NAT in our dedicated account. We'll outline the options in the diagram.
[02:23] Liam: timeline: we want pilot in July, production by end of Q3, budget is constrained so we may start with a small dedicated pool if latency beats hosted.
[02:34] Sofia: that's reasonable. can you share success metrics? p99 targets, cost thresholds?
[02:38] Liam: target p99 < 200ms for prompt sizes typical to our use (approx 512 tokens), cost per 1k tokens should be below our internal benchmark vs CloudGiant.
[02:47] Marco: good. we'll propose an instance and quantization config for that workload in the pilot plan. Also will include a plan for prefix caching and batching to hit the p99.
[03:00] Priya: data residency again — any metadata or telemetry leaving the EU region by default? we need guarantees as part of procurement.
[03:10] Marco: our Private control plane can be deployed in-region; telemetry and model inference can be pinned. some control-plane ops out-of-region can be optional — we can scope to a fully in-region private control plane for regulatory customers, but that increases cost. we'll document tradeoffs.
[03:29] Nina: for procurement, we need SOC2 Type II and ISO docs, and clear SLA for uptime. also any export controls on model weights?
[03:39] Sofia: we have SOC2 and ISO attestation docs; we'll attach them. model licensing depends on model choice — open models are fine, but for some proprietary variants there may be different licenses.
[03:52] Daniel: question on DNS — if we use PrivateLink endpoints, do you recommend private hosted zone entries? how do you handle DNS split-horizon?
[04:01] Marco: yes, typically we recommend creating private hosted zones in your VPC and pointing service domain names to the interface endpoints. we provide guidance for split-horizon to avoid leakage. we'll include terraform snippets.
[04:13] Liam: good. are there any throughput limits per endpoint? we run bursts at certain times.
[04:19] Marco: there are soft limits; with Dedicated pools we guarantee throughput via reserved capacity. for Private, you can configure reserved capacity or autoscaling pools. We'll show sizing guidance based on tokens per second.
[04:34] Sofia: can you walk us through a simple flow: a request from Elmcrest app -> hits interface endpoint -> reaches Redwood worker -> calls model -> back? and where does the KV cache live?
[04:45] Marco: sure, diagram verbally: Elmcrest app in eu-west-1 calls the PrivateLink endpoint (interface ENI) -> traffic goes to Redwood worker nodes (deployed in your VPC/peered VPC) -> runtime reads KV cache; cache can be co-located on the worker group or in a managed Redis inside your network — depends on latency requirements. We prefer local KV for p99-sensitive workloads.
[05:09] Priya: weird question: do you keep transient model context or logs with identifiable data? we need redaction or retention policies.
[05:20] Sofia: by default, Private gives you full control; we can turn off retention and only store necessary telemetry. during pilot we'll agree on retention windows and redaction options.
[05:30] Daniel: for network debugging during pilot, can you provide packet-level logs or flow logs?
[05:36] Marco: we'll provide flow-level logs and extensive tracing; packet capture is sensitive but we can work with your network team under an NDA if needed.
[05:46] Liam: Procurement question — pricing model for Private? committed reserved vs usage?
[05:51] Sofia: Private is usually packaged as a platform fee + reserved GPU capacity option. you can start with a small reserved pool for Q3 and we can enable autoscale for bursts. we'll propose a pilot price.
[06:02] Nina: what's the procurement lead time for dedicated GPUs? we need to know contract start dates to align budgeting.
[06:08] Sofia: lead time depends on region and availability; typical ramp is 2-4 weeks after contract signature to spin up a dedicated pool, less if you're using existing infra in your VPC.
[06:18] Marco: just adding, if you're deploying in your own VPC the provisioning is faster because we don't need to allocate cross-account infra.
[06:24] Liam: are there known issues with AWS PrivateLink and cross-account DNS? we have multiple accounts; this could complicate setup.
[06:32] Marco: cross-account is common; we provide guidance. often customers use a shared services account with Transit Gateway or use VPC peering where appropriate. we'll give a matrix of patterns.
[06:44] Sofia: any regulatory or customer partners requiring IP allowlists? you mentioned partners earlier.
[06:49] Liam: yes, a couple EU partners insist on fixed source IPs for webhook callbacks.
[06:54] Marco: options: establish a NAT gateway in Elmcrest account with Elastic IPs for egress, or we can proxy egress through a static egress cluster in a pinned region. We'll detail pros/cons.
[07:06] Priya: encryption in transit — TLS mutual?
[07:09] Marco: mutual TLS is supported for private endpoints; we can terminate at your gateway if you prefer.
[07:15] Daniel: curious about maintenance windows and how rollouts happen for model versions — we need predictable windows for our SLAs.
[07:23] Marco: rollouts can be orchestrated with canary flows; for Private we give you control over scheduling. automatic fallback to older model versions is supported too.
[07:34] Sofia: this is a good point for pilot acceptance criteria: production-like p99, static egress for partner, in-region residency, and security attestation. is that fair?
[07:42] Liam: yes, make that the pilot gating criteria.
[07:45] Marco: note on monitoring — we attach route-level tracing and token-level cost breakdowns so you can see per-request cost.
[07:55] Priya: what about RBAC and SSO for accessing the console and APIs? we need SAML SSO and role-based access for teams.
[08:03] Sofia: we support SAML and OIDC, and RBAC with roles that align to ops, dev, and security. we'll include docs on SCIM and provisioning.
[08:11] Nina: procurement timeline question again — if pilot is July, contracts need to be in place by early July?
[08:18] Sofia: yes, we'll aim to get the SOW and pilot agreement signed week of July 1st.
[08:24] Liam: can you talk about outages and fallback — if your private cluster in our VPC has an issue, can we fail over to hosted Redwood?
[08:34] Marco: failing over from Private to Hosted is supported depending on networking. we can set up an automated fallback policy to route requests to a hosted endpoint in a different region; there's an ops playbook for graceful degradation.
[08:46] Daniel: any additional ports/protocols we need to open aside from HTTPS?
[08:51] Marco: generally HTTPS + management ports for optional agents; we'll list exact ports. for interface endpoints you only need ENI traffic.
[08:59] Priya: about evidence for compliance — will you provide logs suitable for audits?
[09:05] Sofia: yes, we can supply audit logs for sign-ins, API calls, and change history; retention windows are configurable.
[09:12] Liam: are there customers with similar setups in aerospace or regulated sectors you can reference?
[09:19] Sofia: yes, we've done private onramps with healthcare and finance; we'll share redacted references and an anonymized case study.
[09:27] Marco: on the networking side, we recommend starting with a single-region PrivateLink pilot in eu-west-1 with a reserved small worker pool, run synthetic traffic for 48 hours to measure p50/p95/p99 and then iterate.
[09:41] Liam: fine, let's talk about sample traffic. our normal prompt is ~250 tokens but some calls are 1k tokens. can you size for the tails?
[09:49] Marco: yes, we'll size both median and tail; we'll propose sample instance types and an autoscale curve.
[09:57] Nina: procurement needs to know cancellation terms and support SLAs.
[10:02] Sofia: shall share draft SOW and support levels; pilot will include a single named CSM and SE support hours.
[10:10] Daniel: ok, can we get network diagrams?
[10:12] Sofia: yes, action item - we'll send diagrams and terraform snippets.
[10:15] Priya: one more on KMS — are keys rotated automatically or is that customer driven?
[10:19] Marco: rotation policy can be driven by customer KMS; Redwood will honor rotation events.
[10:24] Liam: perfect. any blockers from Redwood?
[10:27] Marco: none upfront. will need your CIDRs, preferred regions, and security contact to enable pilot.
[10:34] Sofia: recap — Redwood to share network diagram, terraform snippet, security artifacts (SOC2/ISO), pilot pricing and benchmark plan; Elmcrest to provide CIDRs, region preference, and compliance questions. Agree to target pilot run week of 2028-07-09.
[10:52] Liam: sounds good. thanks all.
[11:00] Nina: thanks. we'll confirm procurement gating items offline.
[11:05] Sofia: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet. end.

Notes on transcript quality: moderate background noise at times; minor transcription errors in product names (e.g., PrivateLink transcribed as 'private link' or 'private linkk'), occasional speaker mislabels.
